rows.function: 1. Move the window as the driver commands, in manual and express mode
rows.failure_mode: No movement or late reaction after switch press
rows.effect: Vehicle: window reacts late or not at all. Driver: feels the switch is slow or the window won't move (clinic drivers reported lateness).
rows.cause: Switch debounce or press-classification time is too long (short vs held press)
rows.rating_reasons: S7: main function degraded. O5: DR-1010 is anecdotal and unmeasured, with only generic prevention. D7: no listed test measures switch-to-motor latency.
rows.recommended_action: Measure switch-to-motor-command latency on HIL at 9, 13.5 and 16 V and add it as a requirement with a limit. Confirm what DR-1010 is.

rows.function: 1. Move the window as the driver commands, in manual and express mode
rows.failure_mode: Short press and held press misclassified (express started when manual was intended, or the reverse)
rows.effect: Vehicle: window runs fully up or down, or stops early. Passenger: a hand or arm could be in the window path when it moves further than expected.
rows.cause: Press-duration threshold has too little tolerance against switch bounce and timing jitter
rows.rating_reasons: S6: express/manual mode is a comfort function. O4: no history, but only generic prevention. D6: tests could find it but none target it.
rows.recommended_action: Add HIL tests with bouncing and boundary-length presses around the short/held threshold.

rows.function: 1. Move the window as the driver commands, in manual and express mode
rows.failure_mode: Motor keeps running after switch release (too late stop)
rows.effect: Vehicle: window overshoots, 180 ms vs 100 ms limit at 16 V. Driver or passenger: window travels further than commanded, so a finger could be caught.
rows.cause: Motor command off-delay or brake timing depends on supply voltage and is not compensated at high voltage
rows.rating_reasons: S7: manual control is degraded, with some pinch risk covered by anti-pinch. O9: DR-1014 shows the cause has occurred. D6: found by a functional test, but none of the listed controls target release timing across voltage.
rows.recommended_action: Analyse the voltage dependence of the stop path and apply active braking or a voltage-compensated off-delay. Add a release-time test at 9, 13.5 and 16 V to the HIL plan.

rows.function: 1. Move the window as the driver commands, in manual and express mode
rows.failure_mode: Express close available while not normalized (unintended function)
rows.effect: Vehicle: window closes fully with an unknown position, so the anti-pinch zone may be misplaced. Passenger: pinch protection may be wrong.
rows.cause: Normalization state is not checked before express close is allowed after a battery disconnect
rows.rating_reasons: S9: pinch protection may be compromised, with no warning to the driver. O9: DR-1020 shows it happens. D5: a test found it, but no listed control targets power-loss states.
rows.recommended_action: Block express close until normalized (WLC-020 to WLC-022). Add a HIL test series for battery disconnect and every normalization state.

rows.function: 1. Move the window as the driver commands, in manual and express mode
rows.failure_mode: Retained power ends too early after ignition off (45 to 50 s vs 60 s)
rows.effect: Vehicle: window stops responding early. Driver: cannot close the window after leaving the car.
rows.cause: Retained-power timer value or start condition differs from the spec
rows.rating_reasons: S5: comfort function degraded. O9: DR-1002 and DR-1015 confirm the cause. D4: functional tests exposed it.
rows.recommended_action: Find out where the timer starts (ignition-off event vs last switch activity) and align it with the spec. Add a timing test.

rows.function: 1. Move the window as the driver commands, in manual and express mode
rows.failure_mode: Motor driven without a command (output stuck on or spurious command)
rows.effect: Vehicle: window moves by itself or can't be stopped by the controller. Passenger: could be injured with no warning, especially a child.
rows.cause: H-bridge output stuck on (driver fault or software state error) with no independent shut-off path
rows.rating_reasons: S10: injury with no warning. O2: no history, only generic prevention, so it is not rated lower. D7: no listed test injects driver faults.
rows.recommended_action: Check whether the hardware has an independent shut-off or watchdog. Add fault-injection HIL tests for stuck-on and spurious outputs.

rows.function: 2. Stop the window at the end positions
rows.failure_mode: End stop not detected, motor keeps pushing into the seal
rows.effect: Vehicle: motor stalls against the seal until the thermal limit, with seal and motor wear. Driver: noise.
rows.cause: End-stop current threshold is not compensated for temperature and supply voltage
rows.rating_reasons: S7: damage and a degraded main function. O5: no history, only generic prevention. D7: end-stop detection is not covered by a listed test.
rows.recommended_action: Add end-stop detection tests across the temperature and voltage corners, including stall time limits.

rows.function: 2. Stop the window at the end positions
rows.failure_mode: Window hits the top seal with too much force
rows.effect: Vehicle: loud knock and seal wear. Driver: noise noticed by clinic drivers.
rows.cause: No current or speed limiting in the last millimetres before the end stop
rows.rating_reasons: S4: noise noticed by most customers. O8: DR-1026 is in the open defects. D6: only subjective clinic feedback, no objective test.
rows.recommended_action: Define a measurable impact limit and reduce speed or current near the end stop. Test it at the temperature corners.

rows.function: 2. Stop the window at the end positions
rows.failure_mode: False end-stop detection before the real end position
rows.effect: Vehicle: window stops short, leaving a gap. Driver: can't fully close, so water and noise get in.
rows.cause: Cold friction or a speed dip raises the motor current above the end-stop threshold
rows.rating_reasons: S7: a main function is degraded. O5: cold-weather stops were seen (DR-1004), but their cause is not known. D6: cold tests could find it but don't target it.
rows.recommended_action: Include end-stop detection in the cold test sequence (-30 °C, 9 V) and analyse DR-1004 for this cause.

rows.function: 3. Detect a pinch in the pinch zone and reverse the window
rows.failure_mode: Pinch stop too late at low temperature and low voltage (13 to 14 ms vs 10 ms)
rows.effect: Vehicle: pinch force exceeds the limit before the stop. Driver or passenger: could be injured, with no warning.
rows.cause: Slow force rise at cold and low voltage, so the debounce and sampling delay the pinch confirmation. The LL-2022-02 fix (2 ms sampling below 0 °C) may be missing or not enough.
prevention: Speed-ripple filter with 30 ms debounce (from LL-2021-07)
detection: Anti-pinch HIL tests at 9, 13.5 and 16 V, -30, 23 and 85 °C (TP-AP-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S10: injury with no warning. O9: DR-1001 and DR-1006 show it, and LL-2022-02 shows the same cause in the predecessor. D3: TP-AP-01 targets the corner and found it.
rows.recommended_action: Check that the 2 ms sampling below 0 °C is in WLC-200. Re-check the debounce-start margin (LL-2021-07 point 3). Consider a lower force estimate threshold or faster confirmation at cold. Run the -30 °C/9 V corner on every software release.

rows.function: 3. Detect a pinch in the pinch zone and reverse the window
rows.failure_mode: Reversal distance too short at 85 °C (146 mm vs 150 mm limit)
rows.effect: Vehicle: window reverses less than required. Passenger: a trapped hand or neck may stay clamped.
rows.cause: At high temperature the reversal is shorter (146 mm) and has too little margin against the limit, possibly from a temperature-dependent reversal profile
detection: Anti-pinch HIL tests at 9, 13.5 and 16 V, -30, 23 and 85 °C (TP-AP-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S9: injury is possible and a legal requirement is affected. O8: DR-1030 shows it. D3: TP-AP-01 covers the temperature range and found it.
rows.recommended_action: Check the limit direction in v1.3 (146 mm vs 150 mm). Make the reversal distance independent of temperature, or add margin. Re-run TP-AP-01 at 85 °C.

rows.function: 3. Detect a pinch in the pinch zone and reverse the window
rows.failure_mode: Pinch not detected (no reversal)
rows.effect: Vehicle: the window keeps closing on the obstacle. Passenger: could be injured with no warning.
rows.cause: Force estimate too low: threshold or motor constants not compensated for temperature, voltage or aging
prevention: Speed-ripple filter with 30 ms debounce (from LL-2021-07)
detection: Anti-pinch HIL tests at 9, 13.5 and 16 V, -30, 23 and 85 °C (TP-AP-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S10: injury with no warning. O4: the 30 ms debounce is proven, but the open stop-time defects show the estimate is not robust. D4: TP-AP-01 targets it, but not with aged or tolerance samples.
rows.recommended_action: Add pinch tests with motor and regulator tolerance and wear samples, and with different obstacle stiffnesses.

rows.function: 3. Detect a pinch in the pinch zone and reverse the window
rows.failure_mode: Intermittent missed pinch detection
rows.effect: Vehicle: some pinches are not stopped in time. Passenger: could be injured with no warning.
rows.cause: Jitter in the sampling task or noise on the current measurement delays the force estimate on single cycles
detection: Anti-pinch HIL tests at 9, 13.5 and 16 V, -30, 23 and 85 °C (TP-AP-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S10: injury with no warning. O4: only generic prevention, no history. D6: single runs per corner would likely miss a rare event.
rows.recommended_action: Run repeated pinch cycles (at least 100 per corner) with load on the CPU and noise on the current signal. Check task timing with a worst-case analysis.

rows.function: 3. Detect a pinch in the pinch zone and reverse the window
rows.failure_mode: False reversal on rough road
rows.effect: Vehicle: window reverses with nothing trapped. Driver: can't close the window on rough roads.
rows.cause: Vibration-induced speed ripple is read as pinch force and passes the filter
prevention: Speed-ripple filter with 30 ms debounce (from LL-2021-07)
rows.rating_reasons: S7: the main function can't be completed. O9: DR-1008 and DR-1023 show it despite the filter. D4: the HIL profile targets it, but RR-04 (cobblestone, 30 km/h) is only one condition.
rows.recommended_action: Verify that the WLC-100 filter and RR-04 are in WLC-200 with the same parameters. Extend the vibration profile to other speeds and temperatures, and tune the threshold and debounce. After each change, check the stop time too (LL-2021-07).

rows.function: 3. Detect a pinch in the pinch zone and reverse the window
rows.failure_mode: False reversal in cold weather without an obstacle
rows.effect: Vehicle: window stops and reverses at about 150 mm, also in express mode. Driver: can't close the window, but the second try works.
rows.cause: Stiff, cold regulator raises motor current and force estimate with no temperature compensation of the baseline
prevention: Speed-ripple filter with 30 ms debounce (from LL-2021-07)
detection: Anti-pinch HIL tests at 9, 13.5 and 16 V, -30, 23 and 85 °C (TP-AP-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S7: the main function is intermittently lost. O8: DR-1004 and DR-1011 show it. D6: TP-AP-01 checks stop time in cold, not false reversal-free closing.
rows.recommended_action: Analyse the logged current and speed of DR-1004 and DR-1011. Add a no-obstacle cold-soak test (-30 to -10 °C, several hundred cycles) to the HIL plan. Adjust the baseline compensation, then re-check the stop time at -30 °C/9 V.

rows.function: 3. Detect a pinch in the pinch zone and reverse the window
rows.failure_mode: Anti-pinch active in the wrong window range (zone boundary shifted)
rows.effect: Vehicle: pinch protection is disabled in a region where it is needed. Passenger: could be injured with no warning.
rows.cause: Position error moves the pinch zone start, from counter drift or loss of normalization
detection: Anti-pinch HIL tests at 9, 13.5 and 16 V, -30, 23 and 85 °C (TP-AP-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S10: injury with no warning. O6: drift of 3.5 mm exists (DR-1013). D6: TP-AP-01 doesn't test with position error.
rows.recommended_action: Calculate the maximum position error at the zone boundary. Add margin to the zone and run anti-pinch tests with injected position offsets.

rows.function: 4. Keep track of window position
rows.failure_mode: Position drifts over repeated cycles (3.5 mm at the top after 200 cycles)
rows.effect: Vehicle: reported position and zone boundaries are wrong. Driver: the window may not seal or may stop early.
rows.cause: Hall pulses are lost or double-counted at reversals or when the motor coasts after the stop command
rows.rating_reasons: S7: position is a main function input. O9: DR-1013 shows it. D5: an endurance test found it, with some conditions not covered.
rows.recommended_action: Count the pulses after motor stop and at direction change. Re-normalize at each end stop. Add a drift test of 1000 cycles over the temperature range.

rows.function: 4. Keep track of window position
rows.failure_mode: Motor continues after Hall loss (1.2 s at 9 V instead of stopping at 200 ms)
rows.effect: Vehicle: window runs into the seal with no position or anti-pinch data. Passenger: could be injured if an obstacle is in the way.
rows.cause: Plausibility timer restarts on noise or slow pulses at low supply voltage, which hides the loss
prevention: Hall signal plausibility check, 200 ms timeout
detection: Hall signal plausibility check, 200 ms timeout
rows.rating_reasons: S9: possible injury because anti-pinch has no valid data, but the driver is warned by the window not stopping. O9: DR-1018 shows it, and LL-2023-05 is the same cause. D4: the 9 V case was found by test, but only on a bench.
rows.recommended_action: Change the timer so that it is not restarted by noise or pulses faster than a plausible rate at 9 V. Add Hall-removal tests at 9 V and 13.5 V in each software release, with the connector pulled during motion.

rows.function: 4. Keep track of window position
rows.failure_mode: No DTC B1A01 stored after Hall loss
rows.effect: Vehicle: the fault is silent. Driver: no warning, and service can't find the cause.
rows.cause: Fault-memory write for B1A01 is missing or never reached when Hall loss is detected
detection: Hall signal plausibility check, 200 ms timeout
rows.rating_reasons: S6: loss of a diagnostic function with an unreported fault. O9: DR-1018 and DR-1027 show it. D4: found by test, so a test targets it, but not all voltages.
rows.recommended_action: Fix the DTC path (WLC-029). Add a test that checks the stored DTC after Hall removal at 9, 13.5 and 16 V.

rows.function: 4. Keep track of window position
rows.failure_mode: Intermittent Hall signal (corroded connector) gives lost or extra pulses
rows.effect: Vehicle: position error and wrong pinch zone. Passenger: pinch protection may be reduced.
rows.cause: Connector contact resistance varies from corrosion in coastal markets
prevention: Hall signal plausibility check, 200 ms timeout
detection: Hall signal plausibility check, 200 ms timeout
rows.rating_reasons: S8: position and protection are impaired. O6: LL-2023-05 shows the same design issue (the sealed connector is a mitigation for later model years). D6: the plausibility check is only for total loss, not intermittent contact.
rows.recommended_action: Add pulse-count and pulse-width plausibility checks for intermittent signals. Test with an intermittent-contact fixture.

rows.function: 5. Protect the motor from overheating
rows.failure_mode: Opening allowed once above 140 °C (block uses stale estimate)
rows.effect: Vehicle: one extra movement at a temperature above the limit, with motor wear. Driver: not noticed.
rows.cause: The block decision reads the estimate before the thermal task updates it (LL-2024-01 fix missing in the shared platform module)
prevention: Thermal model reviewed against thermocouple data (TP-TH-01)
detection: Thermal model reviewed against thermocouple data (TP-TH-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S6: limited extra heating, no function lost directly. O9: DR-1012 and DR-1019 show it and LL-2024-01 is the same cause. D4: TP-TH-01 compares the model, not the timing, but TC-TH-03 found it.
rows.recommended_action: Confirm that the LL-2024-01 fix (block decision after thermal task in the same cycle) is in the WLC-200 platform module. Re-run TC-TH-03 and add a request right after the limit crossing.

rows.function: 5. Protect the motor from overheating
rows.failure_mode: Model underestimates motor temperature
rows.effect: Vehicle: motor overheats, with possible damage. Driver: window may stop working.
rows.cause: Wrong thermal parameters (heat capacity, cooling) for the WLC-200 motor, or current measurement error
prevention: Thermal model reviewed against thermocouple data (TP-TH-01)
detection: Thermal model reviewed against thermocouple data (TP-TH-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S8: motor loss means the window can't move. O4: reviewed against data, but with open questions on the shared module. D4: TP-TH-01 targets it, but perhaps not at all ambient temperatures.
rows.recommended_action: Verify the model at high ambient temperature, with several motor samples and with repeated cycling.

rows.function: 5. Protect the motor from overheating
rows.failure_mode: Model overestimates temperature, blocking the window unnecessarily
rows.effect: Vehicle: opening is blocked when the motor is not hot. Driver: window can't be opened.
rows.cause: Conservative or drifting estimate, or model state not decreasing correctly during cooling
prevention: Thermal model reviewed against thermocouple data (TP-TH-01)
detection: Thermal model reviewed against thermocouple data (TP-TH-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S7: main function degraded. O4: reviewed model, no history. D4: TP-TH-01 targets it.
rows.recommended_action: Include cool-down and long-rest behaviour in TP-TH-01.

rows.function: 5. Protect the motor from overheating
rows.failure_mode: Thermal estimate lost at power cycle (model restarts at ambient)
rows.effect: Vehicle: a hot motor is treated as cold, so protection is late. Driver: window motor may overheat after battery reconnect.
rows.cause: Model state is not kept in non-volatile memory across resets and sleep
rows.rating_reasons: S7: motor damage and loss of function. O5: no history, generic prevention. D7: TP-TH-01 doesn't cover resets.
rows.recommended_action: Test thermal behaviour with power cycles and resets while hot. Decide whether to save the state or assume a hot start after a reset.

rows.function: 6. Report status and faults to the body controller
rows.failure_mode: WLC_Status frame missing during diagnostic requests (200 ms gap)
rows.effect: Vehicle: the body controller loses status for one cycle. Driver: possible spurious warning.
rows.cause: Transmit queue or buffer overflow during long diagnostic responses drops the status frame
prevention: CAN transmit queue sized for the worst-case bus load (from LL-2024-09)
rows.rating_reasons: S5: comfort status degraded. O8: DR-1016 shows it despite the sizing, so the prevention is not effective. D4: TC-DG-03 targets it, but there is no listed control for it.
rows.recommended_action: Check that the dedicated status transmit buffer from LL-2024-09 is in WLC-200 and recalculate the worst-case queue. Repeat TC-DG-03 with more requests at the worst-case bus load.

rows.function: 6. Report status and faults to the body controller
rows.failure_mode: Overcurrent not reported (no DTC B1A02, fault state stays 0)
rows.effect: Vehicle: the motor stops but the fault is invisible. Driver: no warning, and service can't diagnose.
rows.cause: Software path from the overcurrent detection to fault memory and the status signal is missing
rows.rating_reasons: S6: a diagnostic function is lost. O9: DR-1009 and DR-1029 show it. D3: tests TC-DG-02 and the injection test targeted it.
rows.recommended_action: Implement and check the WLC-030 and WLC-038 DTC storage and the fault state in WLC_Status. Re-run TC-DG-02.

rows.function: 6. Report status and faults to the body controller
rows.failure_mode: WLC_CloseAll accepted when corrupted or unintended (unintended function)
rows.effect: Vehicle: all windows close without a driver request. Passenger: could be injured if the frame is a false one.
rows.cause: No alive counter or CRC check on the WLC_CloseAll frame
rows.rating_reasons: S9: possible injury, though anti-pinch should still work. O3: no history, but no specific prevention is documented. D6: no listed test sends corrupted frames.
rows.recommended_action: Check how the frame is protected in the CAN specification. Add HIL tests with corrupted, repeated and out-of-sequence frames.

rows.function: 6. Report status and faults to the body controller
rows.failure_mode: Diagnostic response late (55 to 62 ms vs 50 ms) while the motor starts
rows.effect: Vehicle: a tester sees a timeout. Driver: not noticed; service only.
rows.cause: Diagnostic task is delayed by motor-start processing
rows.rating_reasons: S3: only service notices. O8: DR-1022 shows it. D3: found by a test targeting response time.
rows.recommended_action: Review task priorities and the execution time during motor start. Re-test with motor start at the voltage corners.

rows.function: 7. Behave safely at low and high supply voltage
rows.failure_mode: Undervoltage not detected in time, so the motor keeps running at low voltage
rows.effect: Vehicle: the motor operates outside the valid range and anti-pinch timing is not met. Passenger: pinch risk.
rows.cause: Wrong supply threshold or ADC tolerance, or filter delay in the supply measurement
detection: Anti-pinch HIL tests at 9, 13.5 and 16 V, -30, 23 and 85 °C (TP-AP-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S9: possible injury if the timing is lost. O3: DR-1025 shows a 21 ms stop vs a 50 ms limit, so margin exists. D5: tests cover some voltage levels only.
rows.recommended_action: Test the threshold with slow ramps and fast dips, plus ADC tolerance, in HIL.

rows.function: 7. Behave safely at low and high supply voltage
rows.failure_mode: Reset or brown-out of the controller during motor start
rows.effect: Vehicle: the motor stops mid-travel, and the position or normalization may be lost. Driver: window stops unexpectedly.
rows.cause: Inrush current (14 A for 40 ms at 16 V) with a weak battery pulls the supply below the reset threshold
rows.rating_reasons: S8: the window can't be moved or closed. O5: DR-1028 shows high inrush but there is no limit in the spec and no reset seen. D6: no listed test starts the motor on a weak supply.
rows.recommended_action: Define an inrush limit, add a soft-start, and test motor starts at 6 to 9 V with source impedance.

rows.function: 7. Behave safely at low and high supply voltage
rows.failure_mode: Controller dead after reverse polarity
rows.effect: Vehicle: the window does not move at all. Driver: can't operate the window.
rows.cause: Protection diode D3 is open after -14 V for 60 s (underrated for the reverse current or duration)
rows.rating_reasons: S8: main function lost. O9: DR-1024 shows it. D3: a reverse-polarity test targeted it.
rows.recommended_action: Re-dimension D3 for the reverse current and duration, or add a fuse or MOSFET protection. Repeat the 60 s test.

rows.function: 7. Behave safely at low and high supply voltage
rows.failure_mode: Mode flips between full function and manual-only near the threshold
rows.effect: Vehicle: express and anti-pinch availability change repeatedly. Driver: window works inconsistently.
rows.cause: No hysteresis or filtering on the mode thresholds (WLC-001 to WLC-003)
rows.rating_reasons: S6: express mode is intermittently lost. O4: no history, generic prevention. D6: no listed test sweeps the supply slowly around the thresholds.
rows.recommended_action: Add threshold hysteresis and a HIL test with slow and noisy supply ramps through all thresholds.

rows.effect: Vehicle: window reverses less than required. Passenger: a trapped hand or neck may stay clamped.
rows.cause: At high temperature the reversal is shorter (146 mm) and has too little margin against the limit, possibly from a temperature-dependent reversal profile
detection: Anti-pinch HIL tests at 9, 13.5 and 16 V, -30, 23 and 85 °C (TP-AP-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S9: injury is possible and a legal requirement is affected. O8: DR-1030 shows it. D3: TP-AP-01 covers the temperature range and found it.
rows.recommended_action: Check the limit direction in v1.3 (146 mm vs 150 mm). Make the reversal distance independent of temperature, or add margin. Re-run TP-AP-01 at 85 °C.

rows.function: 6. Report status and faults to the body controller
rows.failure_mode: WLC_CloseAll accepted when corrupted or unintended (unintended function)
rows.effect: Vehicle: all windows close without a driver request. Passenger: could be injured if the frame is a false one.
rows.cause: No alive counter or CRC check on the WLC_CloseAll frame
rows.rating_reasons: S9: possible injury, though anti-pinch should still work. O3: no history, but no specific prevention is documented. D6: no listed test sends corrupted frames.
rows.recommended_action: Check how the frame is protected in the CAN specification. Add HIL tests with corrupted, repeated and out-of-sequence frames.

rows.function: 7. Behave safely at low and high supply voltage
rows.failure_mode: Undervoltage not detected in time, so the motor keeps running at low voltage
rows.effect: Vehicle: the motor operates outside the valid range and anti-pinch timing is not met. Passenger: pinch risk.
rows.cause: Wrong supply threshold or ADC tolerance, or filter delay in the supply measurement
detection: Anti-pinch HIL tests at 9, 13.5 and 16 V, -30, 23 and 85 °C (TP-AP-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S9: possible injury if the timing is lost. O3: DR-1025 shows a 21 ms stop vs a 50 ms limit, so margin exists. D5: tests cover some voltage levels only.
rows.recommended_action: Test the threshold with slow ramps and fast dips, plus ADC tolerance, in HIL.

rows.function: 4. Keep track of window position
rows.failure_mode: Intermittent Hall signal (corroded connector) gives lost or extra pulses
rows.effect: Vehicle: position error and wrong pinch zone. Passenger: pinch protection may be reduced.
rows.cause: Connector contact resistance varies from corrosion in coastal markets
prevention: Hall signal plausibility check, 200 ms timeout
detection: Hall signal plausibility check, 200 ms timeout
rows.rating_reasons: S8: position and protection are impaired. O6: LL-2023-05 shows the same design issue (the sealed connector is a mitigation for later model years). D6: the plausibility check is only for total loss, not intermittent contact.
rows.recommended_action: Add pulse-count and pulse-width plausibility checks for intermittent signals. Test with an intermittent-contact fixture.

rows.function: 7. Behave safely at low and high supply voltage
rows.failure_mode: Reset or brown-out of the controller during motor start
rows.effect: Vehicle: the motor stops mid-travel, and the position or normalization may be lost. Driver: window stops unexpectedly.
rows.cause: Inrush current (14 A for 40 ms at 16 V) with a weak battery pulls the supply below the reset threshold
rows.rating_reasons: S8: the window can't be moved or closed. O5: DR-1028 shows high inrush but there is no limit in the spec and no reset seen. D6: no listed test starts the motor on a weak supply.
rows.recommended_action: Define an inrush limit, add a soft-start, and test motor starts at 6 to 9 V with source impedance.

rows.function: 7. Behave safely at low and high supply voltage
rows.failure_mode: Controller dead after reverse polarity
rows.effect: Vehicle: the window does not move at all. Driver: can't operate the window.
rows.cause: Protection diode D3 is open after -14 V for 60 s (underrated for the reverse current or duration)
rows.rating_reasons: S8: main function lost. O9: DR-1024 shows it. D3: a reverse-polarity test targeted it.
rows.recommended_action: Re-dimension D3 for the reverse current and duration, or add a fuse or MOSFET protection. Repeat the 60 s test.

rows.function: 5. Protect the motor from overheating
rows.failure_mode: Model underestimates motor temperature
rows.effect: Vehicle: motor overheats, with possible damage. Driver: window may stop working.
rows.cause: Wrong thermal parameters (heat capacity, cooling) for the WLC-200 motor, or current measurement error
prevention: Thermal model reviewed against thermocouple data (TP-TH-01)
detection: Thermal model reviewed against thermocouple data (TP-TH-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S8: motor loss means the window can't move. O4: reviewed against data, but with open questions on the shared module. D4: TP-TH-01 targets it, but perhaps not at all ambient temperatures.
rows.recommended_action: Verify the model at high ambient temperature, with several motor samples and with repeated cycling.

rows.function: 1. Move the window as the driver commands, in manual and express mode
rows.failure_mode: Motor keeps running after switch release (too late stop)
rows.effect: Vehicle: window overshoots, 180 ms vs 100 ms limit at 16 V. Driver or passenger: window travels further than commanded, so a finger could be caught.
rows.cause: Motor command off-delay or brake timing depends on supply voltage and is not compensated at high voltage
rows.rating_reasons: S7: manual control is degraded, with some pinch risk covered by anti-pinch. O9: DR-1014 shows the cause has occurred. D6: found by a functional test, but none of the listed controls target release timing across voltage.
rows.recommended_action: Analyse the voltage dependence of the stop path and apply active braking or a voltage-compensated off-delay. Add a release-time test at 9, 13.5 and 16 V to the HIL plan.

rows.function: 3. Detect a pinch in the pinch zone and reverse the window
rows.failure_mode: False reversal in cold weather without an obstacle
rows.effect: Vehicle: window stops and reverses at about 150 mm, also in express mode. Driver: can't close the window, but the second try works.
rows.cause: Stiff, cold regulator raises motor current and force estimate with no temperature compensation of the baseline
prevention: Speed-ripple filter with 30 ms debounce (from LL-2021-07)
detection: Anti-pinch HIL tests at 9, 13.5 and 16 V, -30, 23 and 85 °C (TP-AP-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S7: the main function is intermittently lost. O8: DR-1004 and DR-1011 show it. D6: TP-AP-01 checks stop time in cold, not false reversal-free closing.
rows.recommended_action: Analyse the logged current and speed of DR-1004 and DR-1011. Add a no-obstacle cold-soak test (-30 to -10 °C, several hundred cycles) to the HIL plan. Adjust the baseline compensation, then re-check the stop time at -30 °C/9 V.

rows.function: 4. Keep track of window position
rows.failure_mode: Position drifts over repeated cycles (3.5 mm at the top after 200 cycles)
rows.effect: Vehicle: reported position and zone boundaries are wrong. Driver: the window may not seal or may stop early.
rows.cause: Hall pulses are lost or double-counted at reversals or when the motor coasts after the stop command
rows.rating_reasons: S7: position is a main function input. O9: DR-1013 shows it. D5: an endurance test found it, with some conditions not covered.
rows.recommended_action: Count the pulses after motor stop and at direction change. Re-normalize at each end stop. Add a drift test of 1000 cycles over the temperature range.

rows.function: 3. Detect a pinch in the pinch zone and reverse the window
rows.failure_mode: False reversal on rough road
rows.effect: Vehicle: window reverses with nothing trapped. Driver: can't close the window on rough roads.
rows.cause: Vibration-induced speed ripple is read as pinch force and passes the filter
prevention: Speed-ripple filter with 30 ms debounce (from LL-2021-07)
rows.rating_reasons: S7: the main function can't be completed. O9: DR-1008 and DR-1023 show it despite the filter. D4: the HIL profile targets it, but RR-04 (cobblestone, 30 km/h) is only one condition.
rows.recommended_action: Verify that the WLC-100 filter and RR-04 are in WLC-200 with the same parameters. Extend the vibration profile to other speeds and temperatures, and tune the threshold and debounce. After each change, check the stop time too (LL-2021-07).

rows.function: 1. Move the window as the driver commands, in manual and express mode
rows.failure_mode: No movement or late reaction after switch press
rows.effect: Vehicle: window reacts late or not at all. Driver: feels the switch is slow or the window won't move (clinic drivers reported lateness).
rows.cause: Switch debounce or press-classification time is too long (short vs held press)
rows.rating_reasons: S7: main function degraded. O5: DR-1010 is anecdotal and unmeasured, with only generic prevention. D7: no listed test measures switch-to-motor latency.
rows.recommended_action: Measure switch-to-motor-command latency on HIL at 9, 13.5 and 16 V and add it as a requirement with a limit. Confirm what DR-1010 is.

rows.function: 2. Stop the window at the end positions
rows.failure_mode: End stop not detected, motor keeps pushing into the seal
rows.effect: Vehicle: motor stalls against the seal until the thermal limit, with seal and motor wear. Driver: noise.
rows.cause: End-stop current threshold is not compensated for temperature and supply voltage
rows.rating_reasons: S7: damage and a degraded main function. O5: no history, only generic prevention. D7: end-stop detection is not covered by a listed test.
rows.recommended_action: Add end-stop detection tests across the temperature and voltage corners, including stall time limits.

rows.function: 5. Protect the motor from overheating
rows.failure_mode: Thermal estimate lost at power cycle (model restarts at ambient)
rows.effect: Vehicle: a hot motor is treated as cold, so protection is late. Driver: window motor may overheat after battery reconnect.
rows.cause: Model state is not kept in non-volatile memory across resets and sleep
rows.rating_reasons: S7: motor damage and loss of function. O5: no history, generic prevention. D7: TP-TH-01 doesn't cover resets.
rows.recommended_action: Test thermal behaviour with power cycles and resets while hot. Decide whether to save the state or assume a hot start after a reset.

rows.function: 2. Stop the window at the end positions
rows.failure_mode: False end-stop detection before the real end position
rows.effect: Vehicle: window stops short, leaving a gap. Driver: can't fully close, so water and noise get in.
rows.cause: Cold friction or a speed dip raises the motor current above the end-stop threshold
rows.rating_reasons: S7: a main function is degraded. O5: cold-weather stops were seen (DR-1004), but their cause is not known. D6: cold tests could find it but don't target it.
rows.recommended_action: Include end-stop detection in the cold test sequence (-30 °C, 9 V) and analyse DR-1004 for this cause.

rows.function: 5. Protect the motor from overheating
rows.failure_mode: Model overestimates temperature, blocking the window unnecessarily
rows.effect: Vehicle: opening is blocked when the motor is not hot. Driver: window can't be opened.
rows.cause: Conservative or drifting estimate, or model state not decreasing correctly during cooling
prevention: Thermal model reviewed against thermocouple data (TP-TH-01)
detection: Thermal model reviewed against thermocouple data (TP-TH-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S7: main function degraded. O4: reviewed model, no history. D4: TP-TH-01 targets it.
rows.recommended_action: Include cool-down and long-rest behaviour in TP-TH-01.

rows.function: 4. Keep track of window position
rows.failure_mode: No DTC B1A01 stored after Hall loss
rows.effect: Vehicle: the fault is silent. Driver: no warning, and service can't find the cause.
rows.cause: Fault-memory write for B1A01 is missing or never reached when Hall loss is detected
detection: Hall signal plausibility check, 200 ms timeout
rows.rating_reasons: S6: loss of a diagnostic function with an unreported fault. O9: DR-1018 and DR-1027 show it. D4: found by test, so a test targets it, but not all voltages.
rows.recommended_action: Fix the DTC path (WLC-029). Add a test that checks the stored DTC after Hall removal at 9, 13.5 and 16 V.

rows.function: 5. Protect the motor from overheating
rows.failure_mode: Opening allowed once above 140 °C (block uses stale estimate)
rows.effect: Vehicle: one extra movement at a temperature above the limit, with motor wear. Driver: not noticed.
rows.cause: The block decision reads the estimate before the thermal task updates it (LL-2024-01 fix missing in the shared platform module)
prevention: Thermal model reviewed against thermocouple data (TP-TH-01)
detection: Thermal model reviewed against thermocouple data (TP-TH-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S6: limited extra heating, no function lost directly. O9: DR-1012 and DR-1019 show it and LL-2024-01 is the same cause. D4: TP-TH-01 compares the model, not the timing, but TC-TH-03 found it.
rows.recommended_action: Confirm that the LL-2024-01 fix (block decision after thermal task in the same cycle) is in the WLC-200 platform module. Re-run TC-TH-03 and add a request right after the limit crossing.

rows.function: 6. Report status and faults to the body controller
rows.failure_mode: Overcurrent not reported (no DTC B1A02, fault state stays 0)
rows.effect: Vehicle: the motor stops but the fault is invisible. Driver: no warning, and service can't diagnose.
rows.cause: Software path from the overcurrent detection to fault memory and the status signal is missing
rows.rating_reasons: S6: a diagnostic function is lost. O9: DR-1009 and DR-1029 show it. D3: tests TC-DG-02 and the injection test targeted it.
rows.recommended_action: Implement and check the WLC-030 and WLC-038 DTC storage and the fault state in WLC_Status. Re-run TC-DG-02.

rows.function: 1. Move the window as the driver commands, in manual and express mode
rows.failure_mode: Short press and held press misclassified (express started when manual was intended, or the reverse)
rows.effect: Vehicle: window runs fully up or down, or stops early. Passenger: a hand or arm could be in the window path when it moves further than expected.
rows.cause: Press-duration threshold has too little tolerance against switch bounce and timing jitter
rows.rating_reasons: S6: express/manual mode is a comfort function. O4: no history, but only generic prevention. D6: tests could find it but none target it.
rows.recommended_action: Add HIL tests with bouncing and boundary-length presses around the short/held threshold.

rows.function: 7. Behave safely at low and high supply voltage
rows.failure_mode: Mode flips between full function and manual-only near the threshold
rows.effect: Vehicle: express and anti-pinch availability change repeatedly. Driver: window works inconsistently.
rows.cause: No hysteresis or filtering on the mode thresholds (WLC-001 to WLC-003)
rows.rating_reasons: S6: express mode is intermittently lost. O4: no history, generic prevention. D6: no listed test sweeps the supply slowly around the thresholds.
rows.recommended_action: Add threshold hysteresis and a HIL test with slow and noisy supply ramps through all thresholds.

rows.function: 1. Move the window as the driver commands, in manual and express mode
rows.failure_mode: Retained power ends too early after ignition off (45 to 50 s vs 60 s)
rows.effect: Vehicle: window stops responding early. Driver: cannot close the window after leaving the car.
rows.cause: Retained-power timer value or start condition differs from the spec
rows.rating_reasons: S5: comfort function degraded. O9: DR-1002 and DR-1015 confirm the cause. D4: functional tests exposed it.
rows.recommended_action: Find out where the timer starts (ignition-off event vs last switch activity) and align it with the spec. Add a timing test.

rows.function: 6. Report status and faults to the body controller
rows.failure_mode: WLC_Status frame missing during diagnostic requests (200 ms gap)
rows.effect: Vehicle: the body controller loses status for one cycle. Driver: possible spurious warning.
rows.cause: Transmit queue or buffer overflow during long diagnostic responses drops the status frame
prevention: CAN transmit queue sized for the worst-case bus load (from LL-2024-09)
rows.rating_reasons: S5: comfort status degraded. O8: DR-1016 shows it despite the sizing, so the prevention is not effective. D4: TC-DG-03 targets it, but there is no listed control for it.
rows.recommended_action: Check that the dedicated status transmit buffer from LL-2024-09 is in WLC-200 and recalculate the worst-case queue. Repeat TC-DG-03 with more requests at the worst-case bus load.

rows.function: 2. Stop the window at the end positions
rows.failure_mode: Window hits the top seal with too much force
rows.effect: Vehicle: loud knock and seal wear. Driver: noise noticed by clinic drivers.
rows.cause: No current or speed limiting in the last millimetres before the end stop
rows.rating_reasons: S4: noise noticed by most customers. O8: DR-1026 is in the open defects. D6: only subjective clinic feedback, no objective test.
rows.recommended_action: Define a measurable impact limit and reduce speed or current near the end stop. Test it at the temperature corners.

rows.function: 6. Report status and faults to the body controller
rows.failure_mode: Diagnostic response late (55 to 62 ms vs 50 ms) while the motor starts
rows.effect: Vehicle: a tester sees a timeout. Driver: not noticed; service only.
rows.cause: Diagnostic task is delayed by motor-start processing
rows.rating_reasons: S3: only service notices. O8: DR-1022 shows it. D3: found by a test targeting response time.
rows.recommended_action: Review task priorities and the execution time during motor start. Re-test with motor start at the voltage corners.
